citation: James-Burdumy, S., Deke, J., Lugo-Gil, J., Carey, N., Hershey, A., Gersten, R., Newman-Gonchar, R., Dimino, J., Haymond, K., & Faddis, B. (2010). Effectiveness of Selected Supplemental Reading Comprehension Interventions: Findings From Two Student Cohorts (NCEE 2010-4015). Washington, DC: National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education.
design: School-level cluster RCT; schools randomly assigned within district blocks to one of 4 curricula or control; Year 1 (Cohort 1): 89 schools, 268 teachers, 6,349 grade-5 students across 10 districts (per-arm fifth-grade samples in Table III.7); outcome subject = reading comprehension; grade 5 (Cohort 1 followed into grade 6). Registry codes grades 3-6 but evaluated curricula were implemented in grade 5.
problems: Report has FOUR curricula (Project CRISS, ReadAbout, Read for Real, Reading for Knowledge); registry has only 3 arms. The 3 fifth-grade impact-table curricula (Project CRISS, ReadAbout, Read for Real) map to the 3 registry arms; Reading for Knowledge (dropped from the second-year fifth-grade component due to school attrition) is NOT extracted. Arm->row_id mapping inferred from registry 'coaching' field: row 56 has coaching='One' and maps to PROJECT CRISS, whose TPD uniquely included monthly on-site trainer visits to observe teachers and give feedback (Table II.4). Rows 54 & 55 have coaching='Zero' and map to ReadAbout and Read for Real (assigned 54->ReadAbout, 55->Read for Real; these two registry rows are otherwise identical so the 54/55 split is arbitrary). Exact model SEs are NOT tabulated for the Cohort 1 fifth-grade post-test; g_se derived from reported (2-decimal) effect sizes and unadjusted p-values, so SE/variance are approximate. Reported effect sizes are standardized by the CONTROL-group SD (Glass delta), used here as g (J correction negligible). ICC not reported numerically; do not guess. Two cohorts both measured at end of grade 5 (immediate post-treatment) -- Cohort 1 (no prior school experience with curriculum) extracted as primary; Cohort 2 (1 yr school experience) and the grade-6 follow-up noted per-effect.

effect_sizes.arm_label: ReadAbout (supplemental reading comprehension curriculum vs business-as-usual control)
effect_sizes.test_name: Composite reading comprehension (z-score average of GRADE, ETS social studies RC, ETS science RC)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring 2007, end of fifth grade, Cohort 1 immediate post-treatment)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported standardized impact = regression-adjusted (HLM/ANCOVA-style) impact divided by control-group SD (Glass-delta style; report Table III.7). Recorded as g with Hedges small-sample correction J=0.9997 applied (negligible at this n; g~=reported ES). g_se derived from reported ES and the UNADJUSTED two-tailed p-value (Table K.1): SE=|ES|/qnorm(1-p/2); g_se=J*SE; g_var=g_se^2. Approximate due to 2-decimal rounding of ES and p.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table III.7 (p.118-119) impacts & effect sizes; Table K.1 (p.K.3-K.4) unadjusted p-values; n in Table III.7 continued (p.119); #schools Table III.2 (p.111)
effect_sizes.notes: Cohort 1 (first cohort, schools had NO prior experience with curriculum) end-of-fifth-grade post-test = immediate post-treatment wave. Reported effect size for this contrast = -0.04. OTHER WAVES (not extracted as primary): Cohort 2 (spring 2008, schools w/ 1 yr experience) effect size = 0.06; Cohort 1 sixth-grade follow-up (spring 2008, one year after intervention ended) shown in Table IV.3 / exec-summary Figures 1-4. p-values reported in Table III.7 are adjusted for multiple comparisons; unadjusted p used here for SE recovery. Impact model controlled for baseline GRADE & TOSCRF, demographics, district fixed effects; multilevel (clustering of students within schools accounted for).
